profiles.summary: The endpoint still answers tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748 (block 50,992,611 on 2026-11-27) and no later tag exists, so nothing it runs has changed since cycle 28. tempo main still pins evm2 7c9f3b6d, reth 5537d69 and ruint 1.21.1. evm2's own main branch has moved past 7c9f3b6d and rewrites the DIV and MOD handlers, the word to address conversion and the EXP gas charge; all three keep the specified results. The release signature of v1.19.1 now verifies against a key whose fingerprint Tempo's installer names.

deltas.delta: evm2 main, crawled on 2026-11-27 (138 files), differs from 7c9f3b6d in 8 files. interpreter/instructions/arithmetic.rs: DIV and MOD now call ruint checked_div and checked_rem with unwrap_or_default instead of an explicit zero test before wrapping_div and wrapping_rem; utils.rs: a stack word becomes an address through From<U256> for B256 instead of B256::from(to_be_bytes); version/gas_params.rs: the EXP byte charge uses byte_len instead of bit_len().div_ceil(8); precompiles modexp.rs, crypto.rs, bn254, bls12_381 and secp256k1: refactors of padding and of the MODEXP iteration count. tempo main does not pin this commit yet.

The v1.19.1 archives for x86_64 and aarch64 carry good signatures by ed25519 key EE3C5D41EA963E896F310EC3CBBFA54B20D33446, and the installer script in Tempo's repository at tag tempo/v1.19.1 names that fingerprint as the release signing key (tempoup/tempoup line 13) and fetches it from keyserver.ubuntu.com, where the key now carries a tempo.xyz user id.

cleared.check: evm2 main past 7c9f3b6d (the commit tempo main pins for the next release): do the rewritten DIV and MOD handlers, the new word to address conversion and the EXP gas change compute what the specification and the PoolManager need?
cleared.result: Yes. ruint 1.21.1 checked_div and checked_rem return None only for a zero divisor and otherwise call Div and Rem, which impl_bin_op maps to the same wrapping_div and wrapping_rem the old code called (src/div.rs lines 8-41 and 128-150), so DIV and MOD by zero still give zero, which UnsafeMath.divRoundingUp (src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol:14) and the guarded divisions of FullMath (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:35, 62, 67, 73) rely on. alloy-primitives 1.7.3 implements From<U256> for B256 as to_be_bytes (src/bits/fixed.rs lines 183-191), so Address::from_word still takes the low 20 bytes of the word and the call targets of Currency.transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and 73) and Hooks.callHook (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134) are unchanged. ruint byte_len is bit_len().div_ceil(8) (src/bits.rs line 331), so EXP gas is unchanged. The PoolManager makes no MODEXP, RIPEMD, BN254, BLS or secp256k1 precompile call. Both crates' checksums match tempo main's Cargo.lock.

cleared.check: Fixes in revm-interpreter after 35.0.1, the version every Arc tag pins: does any of them mean 35.0.1 computes an opcode the PoolManager uses differently?
cleared.result: No. The Fixed entries from 37.0.0 to 43.0.2 are: Bytecode::new_analyzed marked unsafe (an API change), pop_address switched to IntoAddress to avoid a const-eval panic (a compile-time failure, so a build that compiles never ran it; in 35.0.1 pop_address is not called inside the crate and the host instructions use into_address, which takes the low 20 bytes through Address::from_word, src/instructions/utility.rs lines 26-29 and host.rs lines 20 and 58), MemoryOOG returned when a memory resize fails (a halt reason only, reached past the memory limit, which the PoolManager's kilobyte frames never approach), and a CREATE depth check for EIP-8037, which the PoolManager does not use (it has no CREATE). The 35.0.1 crate checksum matches the v0.8.6 lock.

cleared.check: L-1165: is the v1.19.1 release that the endpoint and the binary reading of cycle 28 rely on signed by a key Tempo publishes?
cleared.result: Yes for the GPG part. Tempo's installer at tag tempo/v1.19.1 sets GPG_KEY_FINGERPRINT to EE3C5D41EA963E896F310EC3CBBFA54B20D33446 (tempoup/tempoup line 13) and imports it from keyserver.ubuntu.com before verifying archives (lines 441-455). The key fetched from that URL carries a tempo.xyz user id labelled as the release signing key, and gpg reports a good signature on both cycle 28 archives (sha256 dc48656e... for x86_64 and 73b9d16e... for aarch64). The GitHub build provenance attestations were not read because the GitHub API is not reachable here.

cleared.check: L-1175: which builds answer the Arc endpoints, does the value-call frame hook of F-125 differ between them, and can a test set be pinned to one build?
cleared.result: Each endpoint answers one build in every sample, so a test sent to one endpoint ran on one build: rpc.mainnet.arc.io 37812c61 (v0.8.6-rc1, 12 of 12), arc.drpc.org 8e8edb7a (v0.8.6, 12 of 12), arc-rpc.publicnode.com 602eed3b (v0.8.5 tag, 8 of 8). The two unpublished commits cannot be read. crates/evm/src/evm.rs, which holds the frame hook, is byte identical at the v0.8.5 and v0.8.6 tags, and the v0.8.5 to v0.8.6 lock change touches only networking and TLS crates, which matches the release note that v0.8.6 only rebuilds images and updates dependencies for security advisories. The native take cases of pmdiff2 give 300 of 300 Ethereum-identical records on all three builds, so the value-call hook returns the same success flags for every native payout the scripts make.
